lessons.name: Discovering the cell
objectives: State that all living organisms are made of cells, and that the cell is the smallest unit that can be called living.
Describe how the cell was first observed, and why a microscope was necessary to see one.
Compare organisms made of a single cell with organisms made of many cells, and give an example of each.

lessons.name: Shape, size and number
objectives: Explain that cells vary in shape and size, and that the shape of a cell is related to the work it does.
State that the number of cells in an organism is not related to that organism's size.
Identify the nerve cell as an example of a cell whose shape suits its function.

lessons.name: The parts of a cell
objectives: Name the three basic parts of a cell — the cell membrane, the cytoplasm and the nucleus — and state what each one does.
Explain that the cell membrane separates the contents of the cell from its surroundings and controls what enters and leaves it.
Describe the nucleus as the part that controls the activities of the cell, and locate the chromosomes within it.
State that the cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance in which the other parts of the cell are found.

lessons.name: Plant cells and animal cells
objectives: Distinguish a plant cell from an animal cell by the presence of a cell wall, plastids and a large vacuole.
Explain that the cell wall lies outside the cell membrane in a plant cell and gives the cell its rigid shape.
State that chloroplasts are the plastids that contain chlorophyll and give a leaf its green colour.

lessons.name: Cells with and without a true nucleus
objectives: Distinguish between a cell whose nucleus is enclosed by a nuclear membrane and one whose nuclear material is not, and name each type.
Give bacteria as an example of an organism whose cells have no membrane-bound nucleus.
